newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GENERALE BANK H1 EARNINGS DISAPPOINT ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: GENERALE BANK H1 EARNINGS DISAPPOINT ANALYSTS.

text.p: Banking analysts said on Tuesday they were disappointed with the 8.6 percent rise in first-half 1996 group net profit posted by Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank.
"It's not a very good result and lower than I expected," said Stephane Roffler of Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
He said it was much less than the 18 percent increase announced by Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) earlier this month.
"The bottom line is that we expected more," said another analyst, who'd forecast a 12.5 percent rise.
"It's a bit low when you know nearly all European banks are up 20 percent and more," he said.
Most analysts said they expected better second-half results for Generale Bank.
The 15 billion franc 1-for-10 capital increase announced by Generale Bank was widely expected.
"Tier 1 ratio was a bit low at 5.3 percent. They'd want a minimum of 6 percent, and that's the main reason for the capital increase," one analyst, who declined to be named, said.
Mignon's Roffler said the capital increase would weigh on the bank's 1996 earnings per share and on its share price, and recommended selling Generale Bank and buying BBL.
Generale Bank posted first-half group net profit of 7.31 billion francs.
